title: Verification fallback lens mapping is wrong for the second seat in a 2-provider panel

finding.claim: Verification fallback lens mapping is wrong for the second seat in a 2-provider panel
finding.evidence: The new mapping assigns each provider only `list(LENSES)[_i % len(LENSES)]`, but the comment says two seats split the lenses. With two providers and more than two lenses, seat 0 gets only the first lens and seat 1 gets only the second, so findings from other lenses raised by those seats will look up the wrong fallback or none at all.
finding.recommendation: Reuse the exact review-round seat-to-lens assignment logic from `_reviewer_tasks` instead of reconstructing it here. In particular, for 2 seats each seat should own the same lens set it would in review, not a single modulo-selected lens.

code_region.text:
# (_reviewer_tasks): a seat's fallback is the one configured
    # for the lens it would serve in a review round — two seats
    # split the lenses, a single seat serves both, 3+ cycle.
    provider_lenses = {}
    _items = list(providers.items())
    for _i, (_name, _fn) in enumerate(_items):
        provider_lenses[_name] = (
            list(LENSES) if len(_items) == 1
            else [list(LENSES)[_i % len(LENSES)]])

    per_provider = []

    any_success = False
    degraded = False

    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(
            max_workers=max(2, len(providers) or 1)) as ex:

refutation.reason: The code assigns each provider a full lens list (LENSES) when there is only one provider, and a modulo-selected single lens per provider when there are multiple.
